# Create a paid campaign

Write ads a strong performance creative strategist would launch, and when the user wants a campaign,
the smallest test that can find a winner. Do not treat spend, reach, or clicks as the strategy.

## Draft the ads

Draft from the [craft reference](references/ad-craft.md). Give each variation its own angle and its
own first line, open in the reader's situation, and let proof lead one variation at most. Compare the
draft with the annotated [Meta and TikTok](references/examples/ad-sets-social.md) and
[search and LinkedIn](references/examples/ad-sets-search-b2b.md) pairs. Use the matching platform
pack for format and account facts:
[Meta acquisition](references/ad-intelligence/meta-cold-traffic.md),
[Meta retargeting](references/ad-intelligence/meta-retargeting.md),
[Facebook and Instagram feeds](references/platform-intelligence/facebook.md),
[Reels and Stories](references/platform-intelligence/reels.md),
[Google Ads](references/ad-intelligence/google-ads.md),
[Apple Ads](references/ad-intelligence/apple-search-ads.md),
[LinkedIn Ads](references/ad-intelligence/linkedin-ads.md), or
[TikTok Ads](references/ad-intelligence/tiktok-ads.md).

When the user asks only for ads, return only the ads in the requested format. Keep notes on sources
or assumptions short and after the ads.

## Plan the test (campaign requests)

Choose one network, one audience, one offer, and one destination per test. Before cold paid traffic,
confirm three things: the product already converts from organic, creator, or sales traffic; the
conversion event fires and is tracked; and the landing page repeats the ad's promise and terms. If
one is missing, say so and propose the step that fixes it before spend.

Test concepts, not wording. Each concept is a distinct angle with its own opening and visual; the
platform's delivery system does the audience targeting when the creative differs. Start from the
labeled defaults in [creative cadence](references/ad-intelligence/creative-cadence.md): account
structure, batch size, budget split, the decision point, and kill and scale rules. Replace each
default with the user's own account data when it exists, and say which you replaced.

Choose the optimization event that arrives in time for the platform to learn from it. A faster event
(trial start, lead) is a proxy: model the paid outcome from the user's real conversion rate. Format
choices, creator production, and pre-landers are in
[message transmutation](references/message-transmutation.md).

This command plans the test. Real results belong to `results`; never present planned numbers as
observed ones.

## Check and deliver

Run [the check](references/anti-patterns.md) on the finished ads: cut what the facts do not support,
add nothing. For claim, permission, and platform review before launch, use the
[policy floor](references/policy-floor.md) and [format spec](references/format-spec.md). Score with
the [rubric](references/rubric.md) only when the user wants a verdict.

For a full campaign package, run the roles in order: [strategist](agents/strategist.md),
[composer](agents/composer.md), [format checker](agents/format-checker.md),
[voice auditor](agents/voice-auditor.md), and [critic](agents/critic.md), or the
[sequential fallback](fallbacks/sequential.md) in one context. The
[walkthrough](references/examples/write-ad-walkthrough.md) shows a full test plan. Deliver the ads,
creative direction, destination requirements, test plan, and the open checks.

Never launch, publish, spend, upload an audience or asset, or change a live account without explicit
approval for that exact action. A critic pass or a rubric score is an editorial step; it does not
authorize launch or spend. For Vietnamese copy, the public `vietnamese` skill may be named as an
optional helper when installed; no polish pass may change prices, terms, claims, or the destination URL.
